full_text_en:
Fushi Bao Home Appliances Co., Ltd. v. Jialeshi Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. — dispute over patent infringement and trade secret infringement

Plaintiff: Guangdong Nanhai Fushi Bao Home Appliances Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Lu Sheben, Chairman of the Board
Agent ad litem: Yu Liqiang, General Manager, Guangdong Nanhai Fushi Bao Home Appliances Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem: Han Xiaodong, Attorney, Dongcheng Law Firm, Foshan, Guangdong Province

Defendant: Guangdong Nanhai Jialeshi Electric Appliances Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Pan Yingming, General Manager
Agent ad litem: Xiao Wencong, Attorney, Fengyuan Law Firm, Nanhai, Guangdong Province
Agent ad litem: Wu Bangji, Retired Official, Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office

The Plaintiff, Guangdong Nanhai Fushi Bao Home Appliances Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Fushi Bao Company"), filed a lawsuit with the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province against the Defendant, Guangdong Nanhai Jialeshi Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jialeshi Company"), concerning a dispute over patent infringement and trade secret infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The Defendant, by utilizing the Plaintiff's trade secrets, sold to the Plaintiff's sales network electric hot water dispensers that were imitations of the Plaintiff's patented product, thereby infringing upon the Plaintiff's patent right and trade secrets. The Plaintiff requested the Court to order the Defendant to cease the infringement, destroy the infringing products, semi-finished products, and molds; compensate for losses of RMB 2,000,000; make a formal apology and eliminate the adverse effects; and bear all costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The Defendant holds its own patent, which is neither identical nor similar to the Plaintiff's patent and therefore does not constitute infringement upon the Plaintiff's patent. 2. The Plaintiff's patent was obtained by copying others' products and prior art, and has been the subject of multiple requests for invalidation filed with the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office, including one filed by the Defendant. Currently, the State Intellectual Property Office is conducting a reexamination of the Plaintiff's patent, and the Court should stay the proceedings in this case. 3. The Plaintiff's sales network can be found on the warranty cards of each of its products and is publicly available. The Plaintiff's claims are unfounded and should be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Foshan Intermediate People's Court:

On August 12, 1996, the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company filed an application for a design patent with the State Intellectual Property Office. The patent was announced on May 14, 1997, and granted on May 21, 1997. The scope of protection indicated in the Patent Gazette is: The design of the electric hot water dispenser as shown in the front view of this patent is of a vertical type. The upper water storage bottle is of a transparent helmet shape, through which a cylindrical purifier can be seen, with a round tubular exhaust pipe standing behind the purifier. From the front part of the water storage bottle to the upper end of the cylindrical bottle body, there is a semi-arc protruding brim, on which there are two small round warming and heating indicator lights, with a heart-shaped water outlet switch below; from the perspective view, the front of the bottle body has curved surfaces concave inward on both sides, a parallel line at the lower part of the bottle bottom, and a protruding three semi-arc petal-shaped water receiving tray at the front bottom, with vertical stripe patterns inside; the rear view shows the shape of the heart-shaped lid on the top of the water storage bottle, with four rectangular holes on the edge of the lid, and a vertical strip-shaped power switch and power connection hole designed on the right side of the base; the right view shows that the bottle body is placed behind the brim of the water storage bottle (i.e., the "helmet" visor), the overall shape of the brim is approximately visor-like, the tip of the brim is slightly lower, forming a 60-degree angle with the bottle body, the indicator lights are visible on the surface, and the base is integrated with the water receiving tray.

Comparison between the electric hot water dispenser produced by the Defendant Jialeshi Company and the design patent of the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company: 1. The accused product and the patented product belong to the same category. 2. The water storage bottle of the accused product and that of the patented product are both helmet-shaped transparent bodies, and their visual shapes are similar. 3. The shape of the bottle body of the accused product is similar to that of the patented product. 4. The design of the bottle body brim of the accused product is similar to that of the patented product. 5. The design position of the middle indicator light is similar. The differences are: 1. The top of the accused product is a water lid made of non-transparent material; the water receiving tray, purifier, and water outlet switch are different from those of the patented product. 2. The bottle body of the accused product has decorative patterns, while the patented product does not. After soliciting opinions from both parties, the Court lawfully commissioned the Expert Committee of the All-China Patent Agents Association to conduct a technical appraisal on whether the two products were identical or similar. The conclusion was: The GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers produced by Jialeshi Company are similar to the design patent No. 96308427.5 of Fushi Bao Company.

Over many years, the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company invested significant funds, human resources, and material resources. Through a series of marketing, sales promotion, and rebate methods, it established 83 first-level distribution units nationwide, including Shenyang Tianhong Electrical Appliances Distribution Department, Beijing Tianhe Materials Supply Station, and Zibo Lianhua Department Store Station in Shandong, as well as 500 second-level sales outlets, such as Beijing Huairou County Department Store and Beijing Fangshan County Commercial Building, forming a large-scale sales network. Fushi Bao Company took corresponding confidentiality measures for the above business information, including regularly educating sales personnel who knew the company's sales network about confidentiality, clearly defining confidentiality obligations, and formulating an employee handbook stating that "the company's business secrets, technical materials, and work meeting records are all deemed trade secrets and shall not be disclosed externally; violators will be seriously dealt with." In 1996, the sales revenue of Fushi Bao Company's patented product was RMB 100,000,000, and in 1997, it was RMB 68,310,000.

Pan Yingming, the legal representative of the Defendant Jialeshi Company, worked as a salesperson for Fushi Bao Company in 1991, served as Sales Manager in 1995, and resigned from Fushi Bao Company in June 1997. Before his resignation, Pan Yingming had already applied to the administrative department for industry and commerce to register Jialeshi Company. In July of the same year, Jialeshi Company filed an application for a design patent for an electric hot water dispenser with the State Intellectual Property Office, began production of GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers in August, and launched them on the market in October. After an audit of Jialeshi Company's financial books by the Foshan Certified Public Accountants Firm, it was found that Jialeshi Company began selling its products to Fushi Bao Company's sales network in November and December 1997, including to entities such as Wuhan Shanghai Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., Wujiang Mingyang Industrial Products Co., Ltd., Changzhou Shuangbai Daily Use Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., Changzhou Daily Use Small Commodities Wholesale Company, Jingsha Department Store Group Co., Ltd., Wuxi Zhongbai Group Co., Ltd., and Wujiang Zhongtian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. These entities were all within Fushi Bao Company's sales network, and some of them were secret clients that Fushi Bao Company had not yet disclosed to the public. According to incomplete accounting records of Jialeshi Company alone, from October 1997 to March 1998, the company produced 69,882 accused electric hot water dispensers and sold 66,498 units. The net profit after tax per unit sold was RMB 15.36.

It was further found that the Defendant Jialeshi Company had filed an invalidation request with the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office regarding the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company's patent. The Patent Reexamination Board declined to accept the request because others had already filed a request for revocation of Fushi Bao Company's patent. On June 23, 1998, after substantive examination, the State Intellectual Property Office rejected the revocation request and maintained Fushi Bao Company's patent.

On March 30, 1998, the Defendant Jialeshi Company submitted to the Court a patent certificate and an invoice for the annual patent fee, both of which were found to be forged upon investigation. Jialeshi Company also forged a Patent Gazette, changing the publication date to April 3, 1998, the patent number to 97312251.X, the patentee to Guangdong Nanhai Jialeshi Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., the patent agency to the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China, the product name to electric hot water dispenser, and adding a brief description section on its own. After the Court reprimanded Jialeshi Company for its conduct, Jialeshi Company submitted a letter of self-criticism on September 4, 1998, acknowledging its mistake, and submitted the lawfully obtained patent certificate. The filing date of that patent was July 24, 1997, and the grant date was July 3, 1998.

The Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company paid RMB 20,000 in attorney fees and RMB 21,055.20 in investigation expenses for this case, totaling RMB 41,055.20.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: business licenses of the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company and the Defendant Jialeshi Company; patent certificates; Patent Gazettes; the notice of non-acceptance from the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office; the notice from the State Intellectual Property Office maintaining Fushi Bao Company's patent; Fushi Bao Company's sales network, business information, client lists, repair cards, marketing plans, rebate calculation methods, interest subsidy ratios for capital recovery, year-end rebate standards, employee handbook, notices, meeting records; the counterfeit patent certificate and forged Patent Gazette submitted by Jialeshi Company; the audit report; the patent technical appraisal; sales invoices; witness testimony; and statements of the parties.

Opinion of the Foshan Intermediate People's Court:

After the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company was lawfully granted the design patent, the State Intellectual Property Office conducted a substantive examination of the patent, expressly maintained it, and rejected the request for revocation filed against it. Therefore, the Defendant Jialeshi Company's defense that Fushi Bao Company's patent was based on prior art will not be further addressed in this case. In infringement disputes where both parties hold patents for the same type of product, the People's Court shall adjudicate in accordance with the first-to-file principle set forth in Article 9 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) to determine whether infringement exists. Jialeshi Company's argument that its own patent should serve as grounds to dismiss Fushi Bao Company's claims is untenable. Article 11, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law provides: "After the grant of a design patent, no entity or individual may, without the permission of the patentee, manufacture or sell the design patent product for production or business purposes." Article 59, Paragraph 2 provides: "The scope of protection of a design patent shall be determined by the product incorporating the patented design as shown in the drawings or photographs." For a design patent product, the front view, left view, and right view are the important parts. Comparing the GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers produced and sold by Jialeshi Company with the patented product of Fushi Bao Company, there are differences in the water receiving tray, the water outlet switch of the purifier, the bottle cap, the front shape of the bottle body, the decorative patterns on the bottle body, and the symmetrical parts on both sides of the "helmet" arc surface at the front of the water storage bottle. However, these are all local, minor differences that do not create a significant visual distinction. When comparing the important parts of the two products and observing them as a whole, the external designs of the two are likely to cause visual confusion for ordinary consumers and should be deemed similar. Therefore, the GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers produced and sold by Jialeshi Company constitute an infringement of Fushi Bao Company's patent.

The Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company took corresponding confidentiality measures for its sales network, client lists, and other business information. Over the years, this business information has brought certain economic benefits to Fushi Bao Company, giving it a strong competitive advantage. Pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law), this business information constitutes trade secrets of Fushi Bao Company. To provide repair convenience to consumers, Fushi Bao Company disclosed some of its client lists on warranty cards, but the lists of other clients had not been declassified. Pan Yingming, the legal representative of the Defendant Jialeshi Company, learned the trade secrets of Fushi Bao Company during his employment. Knowing that these trade secrets were obtained through the company's long-term investment and that the company had confidentiality agreements with its employees, he resigned to establish his own company, violated the confidentiality agreement with Fushi Bao Company, and provided the trade secrets he had learned to Jialeshi Company. Jialeshi Company used this information for sales activities, thereby obtaining high profits in a short period. This conduct is precisely the unfair competition activity prohibited by Article 10, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Pursuant to Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, Jialeshi Company shall bear compensation liability for the damages caused to Fushi Bao Company by its infringement of trade secrets.

In summary, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on September 2, 1998:

1. The Defendant Jialeshi Company shall immediately cease the production and sale of GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers as of the effective date of this judgment, and shall destroy the molds for the infringing GD601 and GD602 electric hot water dispensers within three days from the effective date of this judgment.
2. The Defendant Jialeshi Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company a lump sum of RMB 1,021,409.28 in economic loss compensation, RMB 20,000 in attorney fees, and RMB 21,055.20 in investigation expenses, totaling RMB 1,062,464.48. In case of late payment, the amount shall be doubled as a penalty for delayed performance, calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period.
3. The Defendant Jialeshi Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, make a written public apology to the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company in the *Nanfang Daily* (the content to be examined and approved by this Court) to eliminate adverse effects.
4. The Defendant Jialeshi Company shall not, within two years from the effective date of this judgment, use the Plaintiff Fushi Bao Company's business information or sales network to sell products of the same type as Fushi Bao Company's patented products.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 23,020; preservation fee: RMB 1,020; audit and appraisal fees: RMB 23,000; total: RMB 47,040, to be borne by the Defendant Jialeshi Company.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Jialeshi Company appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court. The main grounds for appeal were: 1. The *Technical Appraisal by the Expert Committee of the All-China Patent Agents Association* and the *Audit Report* by the Foshan Certified Public Accountants Firm, upon which the first-instance judgment was based, were commissioned by the collegial panel after the trial and were not subject to cross-examination during the trial, thus violating procedural law. 2. The electric hot water dispenser produced by the Appellant has essential differences from the Respondent's patented product in terms of the water storage cup, the handle of the water storage cup lid, the housing, the front cylindrical surface of the housing, the part of the upper housing with the water outlet, the water receiving tray, and the water fetching switch. The fact that the Appellant's product also obtained a patent proves that the two products are neither identical nor similar. 3. The *Audit Report* by the Foshan Certified Public Accountants Firm calculated the Appellant's illegal income based on production quantity and net profit, thereby compensating the Respondent with part of the Appellant's rightful earnings. This is neither factual nor legally supported. The Appellant has now commissioned its own accountant to conduct an audit, which has produced a different, objective, and fair conclusion, which the Appellant requests the Court to adopt. 4. Since the first-instance judgment found that Pan Yingming had infringed the Respondent's trade secrets, he should have been joined as a party to the proceedings.

Opinion of the Guangdong High People's Court after trial:

Both the Respondent Fushi Bao Company and the Appellant Jialeshi Company hold design patents for electric hot water dispensers. However, Fushi Bao Company's patent application was filed first. Therefore, whether Jialeshi Company's patent constitutes infringement shall be examined according to the scope of protection of Fushi Bao Company's patent. Upon examination, the later-filed design patent of Jialeshi Company completely falls within the scope of protection of Fushi Bao Company's patent. Without Fushi Bao Company's permission, Jialeshi Company produced and sold electric hot water dispensers that are similar to Fushi Bao Company's patented product, thereby infringing Fushi Bao Company's patent right and shall bear liability for the infringement. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Patent Law, a design patent should not be granted for a product that is similar to a design that has been publicly used. Whether Jialeshi Company's granted patent should be resolved through invalidation proceedings shall be lawfully applied for by an interested party and is not within the jurisdiction of the Court.

The first-instance court, having obtained the prior consent of both parties, commissioned experts to conduct an appraisal. Afterward, it notified both parties to authenticate the appraisal conclusion and the audit report. The Appellant Jialeshi Company submitted separate written opinions on these two documents. The appraisal conclusion and the audit report are the analytical opinions of experts, and the Court only uses them as a reference for judgment, not as the basis. Jialeshi Company's argument that the Court's acceptance of these two materials did not comply with legal procedures is inconsistent with the facts and will not be adopted. Moreover, the *Audit Report* calculated Jialeshi Company's sales volume by deducting the quantity of products sealed by the Court from the quantity recorded in Jialeshi Company's purchase invoices, and then derived Jialeshi Company's illegal profit by multiplying the sales volume by the net profit per unit sold. This calculation method results in a lower figure than simply calculating Jialeshi Company's profit, which is not unfavorable to Jialeshi Company, and the audit result is reasonable. Jialeshi Company's claim that this calculation leaves it with no profit lacks evidentiary support and will not be adopted. The audit result produced by an accountant commissioned by Jialeshi Company itself, which was conducted under conditions of incomplete data and inability to perform the audit according to normal procedures, cannot be used as evidence by the Court.

The Appellant Jialeshi Company used the trade secrets learned by its legal representative, Pan Yingming, during his tenure with the Respondent Fushi Bao Company to promote its products, which constitutes unfair competition and shall bear tort liability according to law. The right holder has the right to decide which infringer to pursue for infringement liability, which is a matter of the right holder's right of action. Jialeshi Company's argument that Pan Yingming should be joined as a party to this action lacks legal basis.

The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, lawful trial procedures, and appropriate rulings, and shall be affirmed. The grounds of appeal of the Appellant Jialeshi Company are untenable and shall be dismissed.

In summary, the Guangdong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 30, 1998:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
